claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch on the current record because aggregate readiness exceeds threshold and no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, with remaining segment-specific weakness manageable through documentation and monitoring.
decision_criteria: If admissible evidence shows the weakness was disclosed before launch, the gap was resolved, or an approved risk acceptance covered it, the verdict could improve.
If admissible evidence shows the affected segment was not actually a named contractual customer segment or named launch use case, the materiality concern would weaken.
If the current record continues to lack a resolved legal/disclosure determination, certification remains inadequately supported.
General monitoring or model-card guidance is not enough without satisfying the internal policy condition for material limitations.
evidence_requests: The underlying release-policy text or approval artifact showing whether this exact weakness was deemed non-material, disclosed, resolved, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The legal review outcome on whether the segment gap must be disclosed.
The source record showing the two insurer rollout commitments and how the affected segment is named.
The underlying evaluation results for the travel insurance claims segment, including target, observed score, and decision owner.
Any formal materiality determination for this weakness tied to the named launch use case.
specific_concerns: The packet itself says support is qualified and weak, not fully sufficient.
The affected travel-insurance-claims segment reportedly misses target by 1.3 percentage points.
That segment is reportedly named in two insurer rollout commitments, which raises materiality under the stated policy text.
The policy text says non-core or low-volume labels do not resolve materiality when customer commitments are implicated or legal review is pending.
Legal review on disclosure is reportedly still open, leaving a required policy predicate unresolved.
The cited public guidance on monitoring and model cards is general governance support, not direct authorization to waive disclosure or launch despite an unresolved material weakness.
unsupported_claims: That certification is policy-compliant on the present record.
That aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents are sufficient to overcome the unresolved materiality/disclosure issue.
That documented limitations and post-launch monitoring alone satisfy the stated release-policy condition for a named launch use case.
Any implication that public NIST or model-card guidance independently supplies the missing internal approval, disclosure decision, or risk acceptance.
